condition.notes: Follow-on rule: only evaluated when reached via next_rule from RULE_VOLTAGE_LOW_OUTPUT. Not a standalone candidate; the overload fact is an internal conclusion, not a technician measurement.

next_steps.action: Rail is OVERLOADED. To locate the excess load: power off, lift/remove downstream loads one at a time (or use a current-limited bench supply set just above the rail's normal current), and re-measure the rail voltage after each isolation. The load whose removal restores the rail voltage is the culprit.

measure.what: Rail voltage after isolating each downstream load
measure.where: Rail test point, with each downstream load lifted/disconnected in turn
measure.instrument: DMM DC volts + current-limited bench supply (set to the rail's nominal voltage and a current limit ~1.5x the normal load)
measure.expected: Rail voltage returns to nominal when the overloaded load is isolated. The isolated load will read low resistance to ground (unpowered) if it has a shorted input cap or IC.
measure.safety: Use a current-limited supply, NOT the on-board regulator, when injecting into a possibly-shorted rail. Limit current to ~1.5x the rail's normal load to avoid trace damage.

interpretations.if_result: Rail restored after isolating load X
interpretations.then: Load X is the culprit. Diagnose load X (likely a shorted input cap or shorted IC). Replace the faulty component, then verify the rail is stable at full load.

interpretations.if_result: Rail still low after isolating all loads
interpretations.then: The overload is on the rail itself (output cap short, or the regulator's own current limit tripping due to a fault). Check the output cap for short and the regulator's current-sense resistor.

Use thermal imaging or freeze spray: the overloaded component heats visibly under current-limited injection. If no thermal signature, the load may be many small loads summing — measure each load's input current individually.
interpretations.requires_info_note: Thermal isolation requires a thermal camera or freeze spray; not all shops have these.
